name: Tiki-taka (Spanish short-passing possession model)
scopeNote: The idea: short, quick passing and constant possession built through technical midfielders, with the ball also used as a defensive tool and counter-pressing as the answer to turnovers. Core era 2008-2012 (Aragonés's Spain at Euro 2008, Guardiola's Barcelona 2008-12, Del Bosque's Spain at the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012); the window starts in June 2006 because Spain's shift under Aragonés and the coining of the word both date from the 2006 World Cup (exact day not confirmed). The label is contested: Guardiola called it made up and pointless (at Bayern, 2014), Spielverlagerung calls it a mostly disparaging phrase for Juego de Posición, and Vozpopuli says it is pejorative. Statements and sources dated after July 2012 appear only under statedView or as retrospectiveOnly. Exemplar teams and managers are covered in their own files.
openQuestions: Tiki-taka vs positional play: Spielverlagerung calls tiki-taka 'a mostly disparaging phrase to describe the Juego de Posición' and says it is a different thing when possession is an end in itself; Coaches' Voice describes positional play as zones and superiority (numerical, qualitative, positional); Guardiola defines his game as overload one side and attack the other. Label the evidence supports: positional play (juego de posición) for Guardiola's Barcelona; tiki-taka for the popular, often Spain-linked name for the possession style, with Guardiola rejecting it. Tier A/B sources diverge on whether Spain 2008-12 was also positional play; not settled here.

Who coined the term: Andrés Montes (2006 World Cup, laSexta) is the usual credit, but Spielverlagerung and Vozpopuli say Javier Clemente used it earlier and pejoratively. No primary recording or date for Clemente found.
Guardiola's rejection comes from Perarnau's books about Bayern (2013-14), not from the Barcelona years; no dated quote from 2008-12 found. The Eurosport page on the quote was unreadable (403).

Spain changed within the era: Aragonés 2008 used two strikers and a single anchor (Senna) with about 50% possession and little pressing (Football España, Scroll), Del Bosque used a double pivot (55% in 2010) and a 4-6-0 with 59% in 2012. Whether the 2008 side counts as the same model is a judgement; sources call it the 'same identity'.

Width: Guide to Football says tiki-taka plays narrow; Coaches' Voice says positional play uses the whole width. No tier A/B source for Barcelona 2008-12 wingers/fullbacks found beyond Bleacher Report 2008 and StatsBomb-based commentary on Alves.

Marking: no source found for zonal or man-marking by Barcelona or Spain in 2008-12 (set pieces or open play). The only marking fact in period is opponents man-marking Xavi (Real Madrid, December 2008).
Defensive pressing at Barcelona is described by tier C sources only (Irish Times 2012, Bleacher Report 2008); the '6-second rule' appears mostly in Football Manager sites and was not verified.
Possession figures: Football España and Scroll give Spain 50% (2008), 55% (2010), 59% (2012); not checked against FIFA TSG or Opta.

statedView.source: Andrés Montes, TV commentary, 2006 World Cup (via Spielverlagerung glossary; SI/90min places it in a Spain v Tunisia game)
statedView.note: Montes is generally credited with popularising the phrase; the term was already colloquial, and may originate with Javier Clemente complaining about long ball circulations. Possible origin: the Tiki Taka juggling toy (clackers).

statedView.note: Date is the article date; undated claim. Vozpopuli says the term is pejorative; no primary Clemente quote found.

exemplars.reason: Spain won Euro 2008, the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012 with a possession-first model; the label was first applied to Aragonés's Spain.
Club side most associated with the style (68-75% possession, counter-press, La Masia core), though Guardiola rejected the name.
Spain 2008-16; double pivot in 2010 and 4-6-0 in 2012, kept the style but called it 'an idea based on the players we have'.
Spain 2004-08; switched to a technical, possession-based approach around 2006 and won Euro 2008; the term was first used for his Spain.
Barcelona 2008-12; perfected the model as juego de posición but disowned the tiki-taka label.

confidence.reason: Many in-period facts are verified, but mostly from tier C pieces and retrospective accounts; Guardiola's own statements are from 2014; marking and set-piece defending are not covered.
